text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to begin our workup, have you experienced any fever, chills, or nausea alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and current right flank pain, have you noticed any specific triggers for the infections or any changes in your urine like clots or stones? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The imaging shows multiple cysts in the collecting ducts, which is highly suggestive of Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease. To confirm this and assess renal function, please provide your recent serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels. Do you have a family history of renal failure or early-onset hypertension?

REQUEST TEST: Serum Creatinine & BUN

speaker: Doctor
text: The creatinine and BUN levels are normal, which is atypical for advanced Medullary Cystic Kidney Disease and suggests an alternative etiology for the cysts and your symptoms. Given the imaging findings of cysts in the collecting ducts and your history of recurrent UTIs with negative nitrites, do you have any history of chronic analgesic use, specifically phenacetin or high-dose NSAIDs? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound to better characterize the cysts and rule out other structural anomalies.
